newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Azeris, Russian LUKoil, Rosneft in $1 bln oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Azeris, Russian LUKoil, Rosneft in $1 bln oil deal.

text.p: Azerbaijan signed a preliminary deal with Russian oil firms LUKoil and state-owned Rosneft to develop the Kyapaz oilfield in the Azeri section of the Caspian Sea, a Rosneft official said on Friday.
The deal, to tap reserves of over 50 million tonnes, is estimated to be worth around $1 billion.

"Today the three sides signed a preliminary agreement to explore, develop and produce at the Kyapaz deposit," said Vladimir Tumarkin, a Rosneft spokesman. "Oil reserves at the deposit are thought to be no less than 50 million tonnes."
Although the deal was only preliminary, there was a "high probability it would result in a concrete project," he said.
Tumarkin said Azerbaijan's state oil company SOCAR would have a 50 percent share in the project, LUKoil a 30 percent stake and Rosneft 20 percent.
The deal was signed in Moscow on Friday during the first state visit to Russia of Azeri President Haydar Aliyev.
"The deal was signed within the framework of the talks (on Friday) between Aliyev and Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov," Tumarkin said.
Rosneft president Alexander Putilov and LUKoil president Vagit Alekperov signed the agreement, Tumarkin said.
He said the question of how to get oil from the field to world markets had yet to be decided.
LUKoil, Russia's biggest oil company, signed a second deal with SOCAR this week worth $2 billion, further strengthening its already prominent presence in the oil-rich Caspian region.
Rosneft's Putilov held talks with Azerbaijan's president in May, after which Aliyev urged the company to boost its activity in the region.
